office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Ryan Dvorak
incumbent.summary: Ryan Dvorak, a Democrat and attorney from South Bend, has represented House District 8 since 2002 and serves on the Rules and Legislative Procedures, Natural Resources and Judiciary committees, according to the House Democratic Caucus [3, 4].
record: First elected in 2002, succeeding his father, Michael A. Dvorak; he chaired the House Courts and Criminal Code Committee beginning in 2003 and was named Assistant Democratic Leader after the 2012 elections [4].

Before joining the House, he was a senior aide to U.S. Rep. Tim Roemer; the House Democratic Caucus describes his focus areas as renewable energy policy, public health and environmental protection, workers' wages and sick time, and college affordability [3, 4].

February 2023: the full House adopted his amendment to House Bill 1639 (regional watershed development commissions) requiring river work to have a scientific basis and keeping St. Joseph River communities in the watershed effort; he said "The rivers of Indiana are an irreplaceable natural resource" [5, 6].
December 5, 2025: voted no on House Bill 1032, the mid-decade congressional redistricting bill, which passed the House 57–41 with all House Democrats and 12 Republicans voting no [8, 9].

2026 session (per BillTrack50's vote record): voted no on Senate Bill 12 (prohibiting ranked-choice voting), Senate Bill 76 (immigration matters) and House Bill 1343 (public safety matters); voted yes on Senate Bill 285 (housing matters) and Senate Bill 91 (syringe exchange program); recorded absent on House Bill 1177 (child care assistance) [8].

race_context: House District 8 covers portions of South Bend and northern St. Joseph County, including the University of Notre Dame, Saint Mary's College and Holy Cross College campuses, according to the House Democratic Caucus [3].

Dvorak, the incumbent, is seeking re-election; Wikipedia's listing of the May 5, 2026 primaries shows Dvorak as the only Democratic candidate and no Republican primary candidate [7]. Republican Eric Harris appears on the general-election ballot [2, 10].
No debate or candidate forum for this race was found as of October 10, 2026.
Little public information on the Republican nominee's positions was found, so a side-by-side comparison of policy differences is not possible [11].

candidates.summary: Eric Harris is the Republican nominee for House District 8; no campaign website, questionnaire responses or news coverage describing his background or positions was found [10, 11].
background: BallotReady and iVoterGuide list Eric Harris as the Republican candidate for House District 8 but provide no biographical details [10, 11].
path_to_ballot: Is on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot as the Republican nominee [2]. Wikipedia's primary listing shows no Republican candidate in the May 5, 2026 primary, suggesting he was added after the primary, but how he was nominated was not confirmed [7].
on_incumbent: No public statements about Rep. Dvorak or the seat's record were found [11].
gaps: No campaign website, social media page, news coverage, candidate questionnaire or forum appearance was found; iVoterGuide rates him 'Insufficient Information'.
How he reached the ballot (likely a party caucus to fill a post-primary ballot vacancy) was not confirmed.
Residence, occupation and community roles not found.
Search results surfaced a different Eric Harris who ran for Indiana Senate District 8 in 2012; whether this is the same person was not established.

candidates.summary: Ryan Dvorak, a Democrat and South Bend attorney, has held the District 8 seat since 2002 and is seeking another term [3, 4].
background: Holds a bachelor's degree in philosophy from the University of Notre Dame and a law degree from the Indiana University McKinney School of Law [3].
Practices law with May Oberfell Lorber and was a senior aide to U.S. Rep. Tim Roemer from 1996 to 2001 [4].
Ran unsuccessfully in the 2011 Democratic primary for mayor of South Bend [4].
path_to_ballot: Was the only Democratic candidate in the May 5, 2026 primary, according to Wikipedia's listing [7].

items: Voted against the December 2025 mid-decade congressional redistricting bill (HB 1032) and, in 2026, against Senate Bill 12, which prohibits ranked-choice voting [8].

The House Democratic Caucus describes renewable energy policy as one of his focus areas [3]; Wikipedia credits him with authoring legislation on net metering, renewable energy standards and utility accountability [4].
Secured a 2023 amendment requiring a scientific basis for regional watershed commission projects and keeping St. Joseph River communities in watershed management [5].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Dvorak about his challenger were found.
gaps: His campaign website (ryandvorak.com) returned an error when fetched, so his own 2026 campaign statements were not reviewed.
His individual votes on the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) and the 2025 state budget (HEA 1001) were not confirmed from a roll call.

A search snippet described him as ranking minority member of the Rules and Legislative Procedures Committee and a member of Courts and Criminal Code; the caucus page read for this profile lists only Rules, Natural Resources and Judiciary without titles — unverified.
No bills authored by Dvorak that became law in 2023–2026 were identified.
Endorsements: a search result showed an IUOE Local 150 primary endorsement list naming Dvorak; the document was not read — unverified.
